newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rain on way in west Europe, good for crops.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rain on way in west Europe, good for crops.

text.p: Western Europe will be getting rain over the weekend, forecasters said, which will please farmers but is likely to annoy other Britons, for whom Monday is a holiday.

Farmers in the worst hit dry areas of Britain, France, Spain and Italy are all looking forward to more rain, after the warm dry end to this week, and hoping the low pressure and unsettled weather set to dominate will bring enough moisture to help parched crops.
A brief bout of rain last week brought thirsty crops some relief but did little to solve the long-term problem caused by the prolonged dry spell.
In France, dry weather and above normal temperatures were forecast across the country on Friday but scattered showers and cooler conditions were set to return on Saturday, forecasters said.
More substantial rain was in store for Sunday afternoon and Monday, they said.
"Saturday's showers will herald a change in the weather pattern, which could bring in more substantial rain early next week," the French forecaster said.
The UK is also likely to get rain, starting on Sunday, after a dry, bright end to this week.
"Monday's looking like the worst day of the weekend," a Meteorological Office spokesman, with the holiday in mind, said.
Rain may be bad news for Britons hoping to enjoy the national holiday on Monday outdoors, but it will cheer farmers and a water industry still desperate for all the moisture they can get.
Friday is dry, warm and sunny. There has been no rain reported in England in the last 24 hours, a spokesman for the London weather centre said.

"At the moment it's hardly likely to rain for the next 24 hours," he said. "Then showery outbreaks will be coming in from the south-west. From Sunday, "overall low pressure in England and Wales means a lot of cloud and rain in places," he said.

Forecasters in Spain, where crops have been severely threatened by the long dry spell, expected warm and sunny weather over most of the country until Saturday, with some scattered rain over the northwest during the weekend.

Heavy rainstorms through northern Italy last weekend (Sunday April 27) have helped lessen the effect of months of drought, but traders say further rain across the whole nation is needed for crops to fully recover.
